last_done_increment.summary: 2026-07-12: registry cross-checks now match on the business-registration number instead of the company name. Name matching was the real culprit behind the missed Sempio certificate — the food-safety registry lists plants ('샘표식품(주)영동공장'), not head offices, so an exact-name lookup found nothing and we told buyers the certificate did not exist. verified_suppliers gained bizrno and, deliberately, bizrno_source: seven cosmetics rows take the number from the MFDS registry, which maps company to number authoritatively, while nine food rows take it from the company's own site next to the words 사업자등록번호 and only after the NTS confirmed it is a live registered business. That is weaker evidence and the column says so instead of flattening both into 'verified'; five of the nine were additionally confirmed by hand (Sempio, Crown, Korean Noodles, Singsong, CJ all resolve to the parent manufacturer, not a shopping-mall subsidiary). The product win: the live 국세청 closed/suspended check previously reached only cosmetics suppliers, because MFDS is the only registry we ingest that carries the number — a curated food supplier could have shut down and kept its badge forever. Curated suppliers with a number are now checked on every search and a closed one gets a red flag instead of a badge. Proven against the real registries: the verifier rejects a row carrying another company's number ('307-81-02816 belongs to 한국콜마(주), not 코스맥스'), a number the NTS does not recognise, a number with no stated source, and a malformed one. Ten rows (7 food, 3 apparel) publish no number, so the live check cannot run for them — listed explicitly rather than treated as passing. The migration was hand-written because drizzle-kit generate diffed against a stale snapshot and emitted CREATE TABLE for tables that already exist in prod (see the drizzle_migration_drift flag). Green: tsc, eslint (0 errors), npm test 31/31, next build.

previous_increment_2.summary: 2026-07-12: held the 20 K-Food / K-Fashion rows to the bar K-Beauty had just been given — the badge had meant three different things depending on category. The HACCP claims all turned out to be REAL (16/16 backed by the food-safety registry); what was fabricated was the trustScore on all 20 rows (78/82/88, a formula over which certificates the run found, shown to buyers as if a factory had been audited) and the 'NTS-verified' label sitting in the certifications field beside HACCP and CGMP, although it only means the business registration is active. Two links had rotted. Sempio's real HACCP certificate had been missed because the registry lists plants ('샘표식품(주)영동공장'), not head offices, and the matcher only tried exact names — the same weakness the bizrno column is meant to remove. OSOI designs bags and shoes: a brand, a factory's customer, badged as a verified manufacturer — retired (deactivated, not deleted, so the call stays auditable). Apparel is the honest limit: Korea publishes no registry of garment manufacturers, so manufacturer-vs-trader cannot be confirmed there at all, and the operator chose to keep the three real garment OEMs with an explicit unverified disclosure rather than badge them silently. The bar is now executable: scripts/verify-curated.ts re-checks every claim against the registries and the live URL and the seed REFUSES to write a row it cannot back — fed the rows as they were actually seeded, it flags the invented score, the fake certificate, the dead links, and a fabricated factory. It also corrected me: I took roundsquare.ai for an unrelated company; the check passed it because it is Samyang's own group site (Samyang Roundsquare). Prod now: K-Beauty 7, K-Food 16, K-Fashion 3, zero invented scores, zero fake certificates. Green: tsc, eslint (0 errors), npm test 29/29, next build.

previous_increment.summary: 2026-07-12: the 'GloSource Verified' badge sat only on three mega-ODMs, so an indie brand with a 1,000-unit budget was being pointed at factories that would not take their order — a trust claim we cannot cash. Curated four more K-Beauty manufacturers using the product's own method: web discovery, then cross-check against the government registries we already ingest (MFDS kr_cosmetics_firms induty=화장품제조 for the manufacturing licence + business-reg number + plant address; MFDS CGMP list matched on business-reg number). The registry did real work and rejected most of what the web calls a low-MOQ Korean factory: Laonhase advertises the lowest MOQ anyone does (300 units) yet has NO MFDS manufacturing record under that name (exactly the trap our buyers fall into); Factosquare is 화장품책임판매 only (a brand owner); Selfcos and Smallcosmetic have no record at all; OEMKorea/CosKorea/Crescent Seoul/Mayk/Sourcing Lab/KPrivateLabel are sourcing agencies that outrank real factories and resell someone else's plant. Survivors: NOWCOS and Hankook Cosmo (CGMP-certified, mid-size, publish no MOQ) and COSMEDIQUE and CTK (publish a 1,000-unit MOQ but are NOT CGMP-listed) — the notes state that trade-off plainly rather than implying every badged supplier is both cheap to start with and top-certified. COSMAX was corrected, not just kept: its 2023 indie programme dropped the minimum from 10,000 to 1,000 units, so the old 'typically high MOQ' note had been steering away the exact buyer it was meant to help; the seed now upserts instead of skipping, or a stale note would survive forever precisely because the row exists. Critically, seeding alone changed NOTHING for buyers: dbFallbackOutput injected only two curated rows with no ORDER BY, so insertion order handed every search to the mega-ODMs — fixed in a4c4b76 (MOQ ascending, NULLS LAST) and verified against the production table (a serum query now injects COSMAX 1,000 + COSMEDIQUE 1,000). 6 new honesty-invariant tests: a CGMP claim must match the government list by business-reg number, an MOQ must be the company's own published figure or null, trustScore stays null, and the rejected middlemen cannot reappear. Green: tsc, eslint (0 errors), npm test 25/25, next build. Prior increments this branch: GLO-EN-JSONLD-PRICE (8306d94), GLO-EN-TRUSTANCHOR (7abe07a), GLO-EN-PAYHIST (406b411), GLO-HARDEN (a1e8f62).

Merge is no longer a human gate; a red build is the gate. Escape hatch [no-promote] is read from the commit subject line only.

Resolved 2026-07-12 (GLO-EN-DBSEED-EXPAND, seeded to prod with operator approval): a serum query now injects two factories that publish a 1,000-unit minimum an indie brand can meet (COSMAX's 2023 indie programme + COSMEDIQUE), instead of mega-ODMs whose minimum nobody published. Every badged row cites its MFDS manufacturing licence and business-reg number, and a CGMP claim is test-checked against the government list.

Resolved 2026-07-12 (GLO-SUPPLIER-REVET, applied to prod with operator approval). All 16 HACCP claims turned out to be real and registry-backed; what was fabricated was the trustScore on all 20 rows (78/82/88 by certificate combination, not by any audit) and the 'NTS-verified' certificate label (NTS only means the business registration is active). Sempio's real HACCP certificate had been missed because the registry lists plants, not head offices. OSOI — a bag-and-shoe brand, i.e. a factory's customer — was retired from the badge. The bar is now enforced by scripts/verify-curated.ts, which the seed runs before writing and which refuses rows it cannot back.

Korea publishes no government registry of apparel manufacturers, so manufacturer-vs-trader — the thing GloSource sells — cannot be confirmed for K-Fashion at all. The 3 remaining rows disclose this in their notes (operator decision, 2026-07-12) and carry no certificate claims. This does not resolve by working harder; it needs either a registry, an alternative evidence source (e.g. export records), or dropping the category from the badge.

Do NOT run `npm run db:migrate` against production. The journal lists 9 migrations but prod's drizzle.__drizzle_migrations records only 3 as applied, so migrate would re-run 0003-0007 and try to CREATE tables that already exist. Several tables (kr_*, blog_posts, social_posts, search_history) were never in a migration at all — they were pushed — so `drizzle-kit generate` diffs against a stale snapshot and emits CREATE TABLE for them (demonstrated while generating 0008, which was therefore hand-written). Dormant only because nobody runs migrate; it detonates the moment a fresh environment, a CI step, or a new teammate does. Fix: rebase the snapshot/journal on prod's real schema (or reset to a single baseline migration and reconcile __drizzle_migrations).

Seven K-Food suppliers (Ottogi, Lotte Wellfood, Maeil, Monggo, Samyang, Samjin, Haitai) and all three K-Fashion rows publish no business-registration number, so the live 국세청 closed-business check cannot run for them and the nine food numbers we do hold come from company websites rather than a registry. Ingesting a food-licensing registry that carries the number (e.g. MFDS 식품영업허가) would give K-Food the same registry-grade evidence K-Beauty has.
